brief.title: Softmax: Scores Become Attention Weights
brief.objective: On the manual attention path (when `self.flash` is false), see how `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` turns each row of scaled, masked attention scores into weights. Positions masked to `float('-inf')` get zero weight, and each row's weights sum to 1.
brief.audience_context: The learner is in the Attention concept and asked about softmax by name. The target is the `F.softmax` call inside `CausalSelfAttention.forward` (model.py:69). It sits between the masking step and the dropout/value-weighting steps of nanoGPT's manual attention implementation.
brief.scope_note: Fifteen seconds covers one transformation: score row to weight row on the manual (non-flash) path. Left out: the softmax in GPT.generate (model.py:324), which belongs to sampling rather than the current Attention concept; the internals of `scaled_dot_product_attention` on the flash path; the exponential formula; the reason for the 1/sqrt(k.size(-1)) scaling; and dropout behavior.

evidence.excerpt:
# flash attention make GPU go brrrrr but support is only in PyTorch >= 2.0
        self.flash = hasattr(torch.nn.functional, 'scaled_dot_product_attention')

# causal mask to ensure that attention is only applied to the left in the input sequence
            self.register_buffer("bias", torch.tril(torch.ones(config.block_size, config.block_size))
                                        .view(1, 1, config.block_size, config.block_size))

else:
            # manual implementation of attention
            att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))
            att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))
            att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)
            att = self.attn_dropout(att)
            y = att @ v # (B, nh, T, T) x (B, nh, T, hs) -> (B, nh, T, hs)

branches.runs: model.py:62-64: y = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, dropout_p=self.dropout if self.training else 0, is_causal=True)

claim_registry.text: When `self.flash` is false (the manual branch of K1), attention weights are computed by `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, which normalizes along the last dimension, so each query's row of scores is normalized on its own.

On the manual branch of K1 (`self.flash` is false), the scores reaching softmax were first computed as `(q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))`. Positions where `self.bias` is 0 were then set to `float('-inf')` by `masked_fill`. Softmax comes after scaling and masking.
On the manual branch of K1, softmax gives the `float('-inf')` (future, masked) positions a weight of zero. It turns the remaining scores into positive weights that sum to 1 across each row.
On the manual branch of K1, the softmax weights then pass through `self.attn_dropout` and are used in `y = att @ v` to mix the value vectors.

When `self.flash` is true (the other branch of K1), no explicit `F.softmax` line runs in this code. Attention is computed by `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., is_causal=True)` instead.

must_show: The code line `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, labeled as the manual path (`self.flash` is false)
One row of attention scores in which some future positions hold `-inf` after `masked_fill`
That same row after softmax: masked positions at 0, the other positions as positive weights
A visible indication that the row's weights sum to 1
The normalization direction: along each row (last dimension), not down columns
A brief marker that the flash path uses `scaled_dot_product_attention` instead of this line
must_not_claim: Softmax always runs as `F.softmax` in nanoGPT attention, or runs in every case (it runs as this line only when `self.flash` is false)
Softmax is applied before the scores are scaled or before the causal mask is applied (the order is scale, then mask, then softmax)
Dropout or the multiplication by `v` happens before softmax
Softmax normalizes over the whole attention matrix or down columns, rather than along each row (dim=-1)
Softmax picks only the single largest score (argmax) and zeroes all the others
Softmax deletes or skips the masked positions; they remain in the row with weight 0
Softmax changes the ranking of the unmasked scores, or makes negative weights
brief.visual_direction: Open on the manual-path code line, with a small note that this is the non-flash branch. Focus then drops to a single row of scores: the raw scaled values, with the future positions just turned to -inf by the mask. That shows the step that came before. The motion's core is the transformation itself. The row flows through softmax and becomes a row of bars: the -inf cells collapse to zero, and the remaining cells become proportional positive weights. Larger scores become visibly larger weights. A total settles at 1. The viewer's eye should move left to right along the row, so the horizontal direction makes dim=-1 visible. End with a brief glance forward: the weight row heads toward v, linking cause (normalized weights) to effect (a weighted mix).
